video.title: Make $500k/Year with One Email a Week

summary: Chris Koerner has Tyler Denk, co-founder of Beehiiv and early Morning Brew employee, walk through starting a newsletter from zero on Beehiiv (website, template, welcome automation, recommendations, Boost, magic links) and monetising it. Tyler's own 120,000-subscriber weekly side-project newsletter, Big Desk Energy, has generated about $500k: $5-7k per sponsored send, ~$80k per $10,000-a-head founder mastermind in Costa Rica, and $10-25k from Boost. Both argue niche lists (even 500-5,000 high-value readers) can earn well through sponsorships, events or consulting, and that paid acquisition at ~$1.45-2.50 per subscriber becomes a flywheel when Boost/recommendation income and sponsorships return more. Chris shows how he segments his list and uses surveys to build a media kit. The episode is effectively promotional for Beehiiv.

tactics.name: Zero-to-launch newsletter on Beehiiv
steps: Sign up and name the publication
Pick a website template (or AI-generate from a screenshot)
Add a subscribe form
Choose an email template
Create a welcome automation; add a branch for non-openers after 7 days
Publish weekly, not daily, to avoid burnout

quote.text: So start weekly and as you grow in scale and and find opportunities to monetize, then you can always ramp that up to to daily.
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

tactics.name: Lead magnet with automated delivery
steps: Create a valuable asset (e.g. your fundraising seed deck)
Build a dedicated subscribe page
Promote on X, LinkedIn and ads
Trigger an automation that emails the asset on signup

tactics.name: Free growth via recommendation swaps
steps: Recommend up to four similar-sized newsletters in your niche
They get notified and often recommend back
Use magic links in friends' newsletters for one-click subscribes

quote.text: recommendations is a free way to be able to get other people in the ecosystem referring you.
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

tactics.name: Boost and ads flywheel
steps: Acquire subscribers via Facebook ads (~$1.45-2) or Boost offers (~$2.50)
Apply to paying Boost offers in your niche and recommend them to new subscribers ($1-3 each)
Sell sponsorships and ad network placements
Reinvest income in growth, raising sponsor rates as the list grows

quote.text: I want income in. I take that income and revenue and I put that right back into Facebook ads and boost to grow faster.
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

tactics.name: Survey-driven media kit
steps: Send new subscribers a survey (role, skills, birth year, goals, revenue)
Segment by answers
Build a media kit with audience data, ad format (150 words) and case studies (41 demos, 1.7% CTR)
Use it to charge $5-7k per send

quote.text: I was able to take this first party data that I've collected and turn it into a great slide to help sell my audience.
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

tactics.name: Goal reminder automation
steps: Ask subscribers their 12-month goal at signup
Email them their own answer 12 months later
One of the most engaged emails

tactics.name: Segment the list for permissioned extra emails
steps: Ask the whole list to opt into a 'focus group'
Send polls on content ideas to that segment only
Segment by listening frequency, investment capacity etc. to target offers

quote.text: I just firmly believe that the more you segment your list, the more money you make.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Monetise an audience with high-ticket events
steps: Understand what the audience wants (founders want to meet founders)
Run a vetted $10,000 mastermind retreat
Need only ~8 attendees from a 120k list

quote.text: all I need of those 120,000 readers is eight people to have interest in going to this founder mastermind
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

warnings.warning: Don't start with a daily newsletter; it's a grind and leads to quitting.

quote.text: Do not kill yourself by trying to do daily.
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

warnings.warning: Emailing invalid or non-opted-in addresses raises bounce rates and risks being kicked off the platform; in the UK, marketing emails also need prior consent under PECR.
Big established newsletters rarely reciprocate recommendations to tiny new ones.
Advice comes from Beehiiv's co-founder demonstrating Beehiiv, and Beehiiv sponsors the show, so platform claims are promotional.
Mass-market newsletters are harder to scale than niche ones for most people.

quote.text: I think for most people mass market is more difficult to do and it's harder to scale.
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

lessons.lesson: List quality beats size: 5,000 CFOs can be worth more than millions of general readers.

quote.text: if you actually can reliably get in front of CFOs that trust you, the amount of software and things that you can sell to that cohort is so valuable.
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

lessons.lesson: Work backwards from who would pay to reach your audience before choosing a niche.

quote.text: it's who would pay to get in front of the audience that I have
quote.speaker: Tyler Denk

lessons.lesson: Monetise beyond ads: events, consulting and experiences can far exceed per-subscriber ad income.
Know your subscriber acquisition cost and lifetime value; when LTV is several times CAC, paid growth is a flywheel.
First-party survey data turns an audience into a sellable media kit and lets you raise prices.
Design should be either deliberately ugly/ironic or genuinely beautiful, not in between.

quote.text: I think in web design you can't be in the middle.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Readers don't notice a missed week as much as creators fear; consistency is about not quitting.

quote.text: we don't occupy as much real estate in our subscribers brain as we like to think that we do.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Owning an audience creates optionality for many monetisation routes.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific dashboards and revenue breakdowns, but heavily promotional (guest co-founded the platform demonstrated) and revenue is lifetime, not audited.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Tyler Denk is Beehiiv's co-founder; Beehiiv sponsors Chris's show; links to Beehiiv throughout.
